_doc: Claude adjudication of the round-6 hunt labels, written BEFORE any case is run through any checker. Two blind sonnet judges per case (a LITERAL copy-editor lens and an ORDINARY-reader lens) labelled every case U/F/B from an anonymised, shuffled, label-free copy (workflow wf_7b10b0a2-eaa). 68 of 204 were unanimous with the skeptic. The rule, fixed before any run and applied mechanically: a U case becomes B if the skeptic flagged it arguable, or EITHER judge read it as supported (F), or BOTH judges read it as either-way (B); an F case becomes B if either judge read it as unsupported or both read it as either-way; every other case keeps the skeptic's label (so a U case with one judge U and one judge B stays U). B is counted in the strict reading only, as in rounds 3, 4 and 5. The judge prompt is round 5's, with glosses added for the three relations round 6 uses that round 5 did not (sibling, headquarters_location, the 40-character contains-administrative-territory property) and one neutral line saying that some items hold more than one sentence and are read as one reply.

bar3_count_note: The skeptic wrote 151 expect-U inputs, which meets AMENDMENT 4's input count (at least 100). After this adjudication 17 cases are U; bar 3 is 0 of those 17 kept at all seven seeds through both entries, every arm VALID. The one-sided 95% upper bound at 0 kept is 3/17 = 17.6%. Of the 151 expect-U inputs, 81 were read F by both judges and 30 B by both; under the relabel rule all of those are B, so bar 3's U count is small and its bound is wide. The strict reading, which counts every kept B case, is reported beside it.
split_rule: round 3's split rule applies to the split_context_retraction class: a case counts as a lenient leak if the checker keeps a span whose reading within the whole input is denied, hedged or reported
blindness_note: the skeptic's README discloses reading the store builder's sanitize, pick_clean_alias and the _alias_map definition line and docstring, and two result-file names printed in the round-4 and round-5 READMEs (neither opened); the spec and prereg name the tables and their builders, which it did not open; Claude judges these do not reveal the matcher's rules
